author: claude
headline: Gales likely to stop cranes at Liverpool on Tuesday as Atlantic storms build
standfirst: Liverpool faces its worst day on Tuesday, with gusts to 22 m/s from 10:00 to 22:00. Severe to extreme seas across the North Atlantic will hold up ships from North America by 2 days or more, and the Western Approaches turn severe on Wednesday.

port_notes.felixstowe: A short gusty spell on Monday evening from 20:00 to 21:00, then settled. Allow 12–24 hours on anything due off the quay tonight and push releases through for the rest of the week.
port_notes.southampton: Brief gusts near crane limits on Monday and Tuesday mornings. Avoid tight cut-offs on those mornings and allow 12–24 hours.
port_notes.london_gateway: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. A good week to clear releases: speak to your carrier about release and delivery now.
port_notes.liverpool: Cranes are likely to stop on Tuesday from 10:00 to 22:00, with gusts to 22 m/s. Tell your haulier today, move Tuesday collections to Wednesday and allow 24–48 hours.
port_notes.rotterdam: Short spells near crane limits on Tuesday afternoon and again on Saturday. If you tranship here, allow 12–24 hours on weekend feeder connections.
port_notes.antwerp: Gusts near crane limits on Tuesday afternoon, then from Friday evening through Saturday. Allow 12–24 hours on Friday and weekend moves.
port_notes.bremerhaven: Windy from Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, and again on Saturday. Allow 12–24 hours on Wednesday vessel calls and avoid tight cut-offs.
port_notes.hamburg: Gusty on Tuesday and from Tuesday evening to Wednesday 10:00, then again on Saturday. Allow 12–24 hours and keep Wednesday morning plans flexible.

inbound_note: Extreme seas across the North Atlantic, peaking at 11.8 m, mean ships from North America are likely to arrive 2 days or more late. Severe seas in the Western Approaches on Wednesday slow Cape-routed Asia arrivals into the Channel by 1–2 days, so confirm revised ETAs with your carrier before booking haulage.

sections.ports: Liverpool takes the worst of Tuesday's gale. Elsewhere the spells near crane limits are short, and London Gateway stays clear all week.
sections.lanes: Storms dominate the North Atlantic all week.
sections.reliability: Sea-Intelligence puts August global schedule reliability at 49.9%, down 5.9 points on July and 15.2 points on a year earlier. Late ships arrived 6.81 days behind schedule on average. Xeneta measures 29% for the same month. The 20.9-point gap comes from method: Sea-Intelligence counts an arrival as on time within one day of schedule, Xeneta only on the scheduled day. Both rank Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd first and second. With this week's Atlantic storms on top, plan on transatlantic arrivals missing their scheduled day.
sections.advisories: Hapag-Lloyd has suspended bookings to three Philippine ports as congestion there worsens. MSC has restored a direct service from Karachi to seven European ports. Maersk has raised its US inland haulage fuel surcharge to USD 215 per container, and Hapag-Lloyd has announced a North America GRI. Malaysia is enforcing new cargo manifest rules, which CMA CGM warns could delay cargo there.
